promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 8 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: Last week was cut short by heat, short sleep and a work deadline, and your fitness is still there, so do not try to make up the missed miles. Next week stays at about 30 miles, with easy runs kept under heart rate 145 and a 12-mile long run.

answers.question: I missed Thursday and cut the long run short. Should I make up the miles next week?
answers.answer:
No. Do not add the missed miles to next week. You came up about 9 mi short because of heat, 5.5 hours of sleep a night and a work deadline. Adding those miles back would pile more work on a body that is already short of recovery.

Marathon fitness comes from many steady weeks in a row, not from any one week's total. Next week stays at about 30 mi, and the long run goes up just 1 mile to 12 mi. With 8 weeks to go, there is still room to build the long run to 18 to 20 mi by early October, so you don't need those miles back.

new.analysis:
**Heat, short sleep and stress shaped last week. You did not lose fitness.** Your easy heart rate jumped from 138 to 151 while your pace slowed from about 9:50 to 10:28/mi. That pattern means your body was under extra strain. The fitness you showed in early August, like 3 x 1.5 mi at 7:59/mi, is still there.

**You ran 27 of the 36 planned miles, and almost every mile was harder than planned.**

| Day | Planned | Ran | How it went |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tue Aug 25 | 6 mi easy | 6 mi | Heart rate 153, mostly zone 3 |
| Wed Aug 26 | 8 mi, 3 x 1.5 mi at 8:00/mi | 6 mi, 2 reps at 8:18/mi | Stopped, effort 9/10 |
| Thu Aug 27 | 5 mi easy | Missed | — |
| Sat Aug 29 | 4 mi easy | 4 mi | Heart rate 149, mostly zone 3 |
| Sun Aug 30 | 13 mi, heart rate under 150 | 11 mi | Heart rate 156, effort 8/10 |

**Last week took more out of you than 27 miles normally would.** Only about 11 percent of your running time was in zones 1 and 2, and the goal is close to 80 percent. Most of that was the heat, but the recovery cost is real either way.

**The plan keeps your mileage level instead of building it, because recovery is what's limiting you right now.** About 30 mi is close to your recent average. Wednesday drops to about 24 minutes of threshold running, done by effort. The long run goes up only 1 mile.

**Running by effort in the heat still counts as real training.** Heat raises your heart rate at any pace, so the same effort comes out slower. Your marathon pace for 3:45 is about 8:35/mi, and it will feel normal again once the heat breaks and you're sleeping better.

**The plan to race day still works if this week goes smoothly.** You're 8 weeks out from the race. That leaves room to add 1 to 2 miles a week to the long run, plus one lighter week, and still reach 18 to 20 mi by early October. Long runs with miles at marathon pace come back once your sleep and the AC are sorted out.

settingsProposalBullets: In hot weather or weeks with short sleep, you run easy days by heart rate (under 145) instead of pace.
The outside of your right knee hurt on downhills in mid-August and settled after a lighter week and hip and glute work.
You do two short hip and glute sessions a week, after your Tuesday and Thursday easy runs.

safetyCallouts.title: Watch for heat illness on hot runs.
safetyCallouts.body: If you feel dizzy, confused or sick to your stomach, or you stop sweating, stop running, get into shade and drink. Get medical help if it does not pass quickly.

safetyCallouts.title: Tiredness that won't go away.
safetyCallouts.body: If you still feel drained after a week of normal sleep, see a doctor before we make the training harder.
